question_text: Differentiate between latitudes and longitudes with three key points.
model_answer: Latitudes are imaginary lines running east to west and measure distance north or south of the Equator. Longitudes run from north to south and measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Latitudes are parallel circles while longitudes converge at the poles.

question_text: Explain why longitudes are important for calculating local time.
model_answer: Longitudes are important for calculating local time because the Earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, meaning it rotates 15 degrees every hour (or 1 degree every 4 minutes). As a result, different longitudes experience sunrise and sunset at different times.

criteria.description: Explains 360 rotation in 24 hours (1 degree per 4 min) and variation of sunrise/sunset across meridians

levels.description: Explains earth rotation rate and local time variation across longitudes

Mentions that time changes with longitude

question_text: Explain the rotation of the Earth and describe how it causes day and night.
model_answer: The Earth rotates on its axis from west to east once every twenty-four hours. The half facing the Sun experiences daylight, while the half turned away experiences night. This continuous rotation causes the alternate cycle of day and night.

criteria.description: Explains earth spinning on its axis (west to east in 24h) and half facing sun receiving light vs half turned away in darkness

levels.description: Accurately details axial rotation period and facing sunlight vs facing away causing day and night
Accurately describes rotation causing sunlight on one side and darkness on the other

Incorrect or irrelevant

question_text: Explain the concept of timelines and how historians use them to study events.
model_answer: A timeline is a visual graphical representation that displays historical events in chronological order from earliest to latest. Historians use timelines to place events in proper sequence using BCE and CE designations, identify cause-and-effect relationships, track technological and social progress, and compare concurrent developments across different civilizations.

question_text: Describe the town planning, citadel, and drainage system of Harappan cities.
model_answer: Harappan cities were divided into two main sections: a raised Citadel on the west containing public buildings and granaries, and a Lower Town on the east where common citizens resided in houses made of baked bricks. Streets were laid out in a grid intersecting at right angles. The drainage system was remarkably sophisticated: drains from individual houses connected to street drains covered with stone slabs or bricks, equipped with inspection manholes.

Mentions brick houses and planned cities

question_text: What is grassroots democracy? How does Panchayati Raj strengthen it?
model_answer: Grassroots democracy means decentralizing political power to the lowest community level so that ordinary citizens directly participate in planning and decision-making for their local communities. The Panchayati Raj system strengthens grassroots democracy by establishing a three-tier local governance structure where villagers elect their own representatives and hold them accountable.

question_text: Discuss the roles of family and community in shaping a responsible citizen.

question_text: Explain the three-tier structure of the Panchayati Raj system in detail.
model_answer: The Panchayati Raj system operates across a three-tier institutional hierarchy: 1. Gram Panchayat at the village level, responsible for local daily governance, amenities, and implementation. 2. Panchayat Samiti (Block Panchayat) at the intermediate block level, coordinating development programs across a cluster of villages. 3. Zilla Parishad at the apex district level, responsible for district-wide developmental planning, budget allocation, and administration. This structure empowers citizens at all levels.

criteria.description: Details the three-tier system: Village level (Gram Panchayat), Block level (Panchayat Samiti), and District level (Zilla Parishad), strengthening grassroots democracy
